clue.text: Formalised shagging is what brought nations together

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stiff, formal phrase for sexual intercourse
second meaning: the statute that joined England and Scotland (1707) or Great Britain and Ireland (1801)

explanation.surface: A smutty joke that a solemn treaty between countries is really just sex dressed up in legal language.
explanation.walkthrough: The Acts of Union are the British laws that merged kingdoms into one state.
explanation.definitionFit: Union is a polite word for coupling, and the parliamentary Acts of Union merged separate countries into the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Tip of clap-ridden member blue? Withdraw!

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very front, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of clap
a member is a limb; 'ridden' is surface filler joining it to clap
feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: A man with gonorrhoea (the clap) whose penis has turned blue is told to pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'blue' both read as smut, but they are a limb and a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb down is to back off from a position or retreat from a claim, to withdraw.

clue.text: Blowjob, amazingly, is too much for a follower of Clinton

indicators.note: the phrase is more than the answer needs, so the surplus letters at either end are trimmed away

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A dig at Bill Clinton's Lewinsky scandal: his successor would find such goings-on too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Obama came after Clinton as Democratic president (with Bush between), and also defeated Hillary Clinton for the nomination.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama followed Bill Clinton as a Democratic US president, a follower in office.

clue.text: Hiding core of penis in huge rocks to send someone crazy

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it tucked out of sight inside it
something that rocks is shaken back and forth, so the letters are jolted out of order
the core of something is its centre, so only the middle letter is taken

parts.note: the central letter of the five-letter word
these two words together are the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man concealing an enormous erection drives someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder; the N goes after the U of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhinge someone is to unbalance their mind, to drive them mad.

clue.text: Sex covers a variety of sins, so be firm

indicators.note: a variety is an assortment in different forms, so the letters come in another arrangement
to cover something is to wrap round it, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'
the fodder, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sermon: sex embraces a whole range of sins, so be resolute and resist.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to stand firm on a demand and refuse to back down.

clue.text: I love Reagan deviously dropping a disgraced leader

indicators.note: acting deviously means taking crooked paths, so the letters are twisted round
to drop something is to let it go, so that small word is left out

parts.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O
the president's name, taken as written
this letter is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone professes love for Ronald Reagan while slyly ditching a fallen leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel Noriega, Panama's dictator, was once a US ally and later toppled by the 1989 American invasion and jailed for drug trafficking.
explanation.definitionFit: Noriega was a Panamanian strongman deposed and imprisoned, a ruler brought to disgrace.

clue.text: (& 27ac.) It's vulnerable, sex, in the grip of degraded drug

indicators.note: being held in someone's grip means being enclosed by them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: degraded means watered down, and drug here is cannabis, pot, so weakened pot
S is the abbreviation for sex, as on official forms

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on sex and on low-grade dope is in a fragile state.
explanation.walkthrough: In drug slang pot is cannabis; the single letter for sex is lodged between the two words of the degraded-drug phrase rather than wrapping either one.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak spot is the place where something is exposed to attack or failure, the point at which it is vulnerable.

clue.text: Was successful restraining Lib Dem movement (the black hole of British hopes?)

definitions.text: the black hole of British hopes

indicators.note: movement shifts things from where they were, so the letters change places
to restrain is to hold something in, so the shuffled piece is held inside

parts.note: to have been successful is to have won
the party's short name is the fodder

explanation.surface: The Liberal Democrats' winning party being held back, with a jibe at hopeless British ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon, the London tennis championship, was long where British hopes of a home champion went to die.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wimbledon tennis tournament swallowed British hopes year after year, with no home men's champion from 1936 until 2013.

clue.text: Stupid as a primate

explanation.surface: As thick as a monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Apish literally means ape-like, and by extension describes foolish or idiotic behaviour.

clue.text: They've quite a bite, Parisian strays — hard for one

indicators.note: things that stray wander out of place, so these letters drift into a new order
one thing standing in for another means swapping one letter for a different one

parts.note: taken as written
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
the Roman numeral for one, swapped out of the word

explanation.surface: Stray dogs in Paris that bite hard.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Is in PARISIAN is replaced by H before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Piranhas are South American fish famous for their razor-sharp teeth and savage feeding.

clue.text: Carry on Nurse's middle bit has Cyclops arse over tip, in a spin

indicators.note: the middle bit of a word is its central letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the central letter of nurse

indicators.note: falling arse over tip means turning head over heels, so the word is turned back to front
things in a spin are whirled about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter means me
these two little words are the fodder for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A send-up of a Carry On Nurse scene: the setter's bottom upended in a whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry on Nurse' reads as the film title, but 'Carry on' is the definition and 'Nurse' gives a letter. Setters often call themselves by their pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is to continue, persist or stay going, which is what remain means.

clue.text: Get over personal problem on receiving head from Archer in can

indicators.note: in a down-reading or flipped sense, over means turned upside down, so this piece is read backwards

parts.note: BO, body odour, is the classic personal problem

indicators.note: one thing receiving another takes it inside, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Archer

explanation.surface: A dig at Jeffrey Archer, the jailed Tory novelist, getting over his troubles while locked up in the can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, which fits Archer, who was jailed for perjury; here it simply means a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get hold of it or acquire it.

clue.text: Knock off Tory leader? Hague's first when it comes to sneakiness

parts.note: to knock something off is slang for stealing it

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

indicators.note: what comes first in a name is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Hague

explanation.surface: Plotting to topple the Conservative leader, with William Hague, once leader himself, first in line for underhand scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock off Tory leader' reads as deposing the party chief; 'knock off' means steal and 'leader' picks one letter. William Hague was a Conservative leader and Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting covertly and secretly, which is the quality of sneakiness.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) He rules from a compound mixture of dealing — clod, oaf!

indicators.note: a mixture blends its ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Abuse hurled at a dictator governing from a fortified base, mixed up in dirty dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' sounds like the chemistry word that goes with 'mixture', but it is a walled military base: Gaddafi ruled Libya from the Bab al-Azizia compound in Tripoli.
explanation.definitionFit: Muammar Gaddafi, Libya's ruler for four decades, styled himself Colonel and governed from a fortified barracks complex.

clue.text: Equal to the occasion? No, vague and waffling, a politician so put!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: alert and ready, competent in the moment

definitions.text: No, vague and waffling, a politician so put!
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a politician placed in an awkward position, cornered by a question, answers no, vaguely and at length

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic picture: a politician put in a tight corner by an interviewer, answering with a waffling evasion.
explanation.definitionFit: On the spot means both quick and capable at the moment needed and placed in a difficult position under pressure.

clue.text: see 13ac.
The sort of energetic type to get Russell off the air?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fiery, passionate agitator

definitions.text: to get Russell off the air?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to sack the comedian Russell Brand from broadcasting

explanation.walkthrough: Russell Brand, the comedian, quit BBC radio in 2008 after a row over lewd prank calls; read in two words, the answer is what his critics wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is a passionate, energetic agitator, and split in two the phrase means sacking Brand.

clue.text: Pigs at home here? "Kettle (right flank) smartish!"

parts.note: pigs live in a sty, so being at home they are in their sty

indicators.note: the right flank of a word is its trailing edge, so only its closing letters are kept

parts.note: the right-hand end of kettle

explanation.surface: A jibe at the police (pigs) kettling protesters: hemming in a crowd's right flank, smartly done.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs is slang for police and kettling is the police tactic of penning protesters in, so the surface is a riot scene; here pigs are just pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in style means doing it elegantly and fashionably, which is roughly smart.

clue.text: In which, eventually, only half of London Games initially organised

parts.note: the first half of the six-letter city

indicators.note: keeping only half of a word means taking its front part and dropping the rest
initially means at the start, so the first letter is the one used

parts.note: the first letter of Games
to organise an event is to run it

explanation.surface: A grumble about the London Olympic Games, only half sorted out eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the phrase 'in the long run', which means eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: In the long run means eventually, over a long period, so the long run is the span in which things eventually happen.

clue.text: Describes one role of prick from university reorganising Ryanair, having no answer

indicators.note: reorganising puts things into a different arrangement, so the letters are reordered
having none of something means it has been removed, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
the budget airline's name, taken as written
A is the abbreviation for answer; this letter is dropped

explanation.surface: An insult aimed at some university jerk who has made a mess of things at Ryanair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prick' reads as an insult for a person; it is the penis, one of whose jobs is passing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Urinary is the adjective for the passing of urine, one of the penis's two functions.

clue.text: Item on Berlusconi's plate: bending to pointless Tories?

indicators.note: bending twists something into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged
pointless means lacking a point of the compass, so one such letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then losing its E, east

explanation.surface: Italy's Silvio Berlusconi has the Tories bowing to him, served up on his plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On his plate' suggests his political workload, but it is literal food: risotto is an Italian rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a classic Italian rice dish, so a plausible serving for an Italian prime minister.

clue.text: Doin' it with accommodating jerk

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room inside, so the answer is lodged within these words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Having sex with an obliging idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerk is slang for a fool or contemptible idiot, and a nitwit is a silly fool.

clue.text: Canine screwed, eating hot Madras once

indicators.note: whatever is eating something takes it inside, so a letter goes within
something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A dog that has had sex is now eating a hot madras curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madras' tempts the solver towards curry, but it is the Indian city, renamed Chennai in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Chennai is the present name of the Indian city formerly called Madras, so it was Madras once.

clue.text: Stink suppressed by Communist Party (the thick end)

indicators.note: something suppressed is held down and contained, so this piece is put inside the other

parts.note: CP is the abbreviation for Communist Party
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A scandal hushed up by the Party leadership, the dimwitted lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick' suggests stupidity, and a chump is a fool too, but the definition is the butcher's sense: the thick end of a loin of lamb, as in chump chop.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is the thick end of a joint of meat, especially lamb, and by extension also a blockhead.

clue.text: Keep your mouth shut, baby, being devious, Ken Clarke style?

indicators.note: being devious means going by crooked routes, so the letters take a twisted order

parts.note: sh! is the word for telling someone to be quiet
the fodder for the rearrangement

explanation.surface: Telling a sweetheart to keep quiet about some sly business, as the Tory grandee Ken Clarke might.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Clarke, the Conservative minister, was famous for his rumpled suits and Hush Puppies shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby means scruffy and worn-looking, the dishevelled dress for which Clarke was known.

clue.text: Shaft Woody's ex? F-off!

indicators.note: something taken off is removed, so the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: Mia Farrow was Woody Allen's partner
this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Woody Allen's former partner telling him, in no uncertain terms, to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F-off' reads as the swearword, but it is an instruction to delete F.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is the shaft shot from a bow, so the word can stand for shaft.

clue.text: Dubya half wants Cameron to turn on Brenda — great!

parts.note: Dubya is George W. Bush, and half of Bush is its front two letters

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so these letters run back to front

parts.note: David Cameron was the Prime Minister, PM
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: George W. Bush is keen to see David Cameron turn on the Queen, which would be great.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda; ER, her royal cipher, is the usual crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper as an adjective means unusually large or abundant, as in a bumper crop, a great one.

clue.text: Climactic reverie of one of Maggie's despised ministers?

definitions.text: Climactic reverie of one of Maggie's despised ministers?

parts.note: surface reading: a fantasy that peaks in sexual release during sleep
setter's reading: Thatcher sneered at her moderate ministers as wets, so this is what one of them dreams of

explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher called the soft, moderate members of her cabinet 'wets'; a wet's dream is the answer read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a sleeping fantasy ending in orgasm, and literally the dream of a Thatcher-era wet.

clue.text: see 7ac.
Certainly not parochial dancing i.e. to Ann Wid——

indicators.note: dancing sends things whirling about the floor, so the letters move into new places

parts.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Ann Widdecombe, the Tory MP, dancing on Strictly Come Dancing before the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes cut off Widdecombe's name so that only the letters needed remain; her clumsy dancing on BBC's Strictly Come Dancing was famously watched nationwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide means extending across the whole country, the opposite of parochial or narrowly local.
